{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-tn","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"f24113848c32a3ca6383ece75f4ca52bcc4362639ac78d1568e7fa81f56735b6","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-tn-class-d:lineage:1","source_registry_sha256":"8b0b6a068a0aa720d419171b5007a2610ed6c5012eeff522b57713cf9226eb71","source_liveness_sha256":"d27b9a94f03ec29d960b8eea38966606a7d3fdb703ad30b19ecd93f9bc70d0c7"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"License classes, eligibility and credentials","heading":"C — Your license: classes, who must hold one, permits, hardship and ID licenses, exemptions, ineligibility and penalties","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Your license: classes, who must hold one, permits, hardship and ID licenses, exemptions, ineligibility and penalties
Knowledge domain: which Tennessee license class matches which vehicle and purpose, who must hold a Tennessee license, how the learner, hardship and identification credentials work, who is exempt or ineligible, and the penalties for driving without a valid license.

FACT_ID: sec01-F01 | anchor: A01
Class D is the license for ordinary passenger vehicles that are not used for commercial purposes, other than the vehicles that fall into Classes A, B, C or M. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-F02 | anchor: A01
Class M on the license chart covers motorcycles and motor-driven cycles. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-F03 | anchor: A01
Class P on the license chart is an instructional permit, issued together with a Class A, B, C, D or M license. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-F04 | anchor: A01
Class H on the license chart is a hardship license for drivers aged 14 to 16 who face special hardship. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-F05 | anchor: A01
The F (For Hire) endorsement applies when a Class D vehicle is driven by someone employed mainly to drive it as a public or common carrier of people or property. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-F06 | anchor: A02
Every Tennessee resident who drives a motor vehicle needs either a valid Tennessee driver license or a Temporary Driver License (TDL). [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-F07 | anchor: A02
A newcomer with a valid license from another state or country must apply for a Tennessee license or TDL after living in Tennessee more than 30 days, upon working in Tennessee, or once they would qualify as a registered Tennessee voter. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-F08 | anchor: A02
A Class D license lets you drive any vehicle weighing up to 26,000 pounds at most. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-F09 | anchor: A02
A vehicle under 26,000 pounds still needs a Class C license, not Class D, if it hauls hazardous materials, carries 16 or more people counting the driver, or serves as a school bus. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-F10 | anchor: A02
To get a Class D license you must be at least 16 and pass a vision screening, a knowledge test and a driving test, and anyone under 18 must also meet the Intermediate Class D rules. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-F11 | anchor: A02
Drivers whose main job is carrying people or property in a Class D vehicle, such as taxi, shuttle or ambulance drivers and couriers, must add a For-Hire endorsement. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-F12 | anchor: A02
People who drive only in the course of another job, such as plumbers, meter readers and engineers, generally do not need the For-Hire endorsement, although an employer may still require it. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-F13 | anchor: A02
Adding the For-Hire endorsement costs $4.50 and requires 2 years of unrestricted driving experience in a Class D vehicle. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-F14 | anchor: A02
For-Hire applicants must be at least 18, or 16 when the vehicle belongs to their family business and is used only for that business's deliveries. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-F15 | anchor: A02
For-Hire applicants take a vision screening plus a separate knowledge test built from Section B of the manual. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-F16 | anchor: A03
A motorcycle above 125 cubic centimeters calls for a Class M license, while one below 125 cubic centimeters calls for a Class M limited license. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec01-F17 | anchor: A03
Off-road vehicles and ATVs cannot be used for the road test, may not be driven on Tennessee or federal highways, and may cross a roadway only at a ninety-degree angle. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec01-F18 | anchor: A03
Vehicles weighing 26,001 pounds or more require a Commercial Driver License in Class A, B or C. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec01-F19 | anchor: A03
A valid Class A, B or C commercial license also covers Class D vehicles, so no separate Class D is needed, but riding a motorcycle still requires adding Class M, as in Class AM. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec01-F20 | anchor: A03
A Class PD learner permit requires being at least 15 and passing the Class D written knowledge test and vision screening. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec01-F21 | anchor: A03
A Class PD holder may drive only with a licensed driver who is at least 21 and sits in the seat beside them. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec01-F22 | anchor: A03
Trading a Class PD for a Class D requires a road skills test, and drivers under 18 must first have held the PD for 180 days under the Graduated Driver License law. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec01-F23 | anchor: A03
A PD holder moving up to an Intermediate Class D skips the knowledge test unless the permit expired more than 12 months before the driving skills test. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec01-F24 | anchor: A03
A Class H hardship license can be issued to a 14-year-old for a Class D vehicle, a Class M motorcycle or both, but only for family hardship and limited needs. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec01-F25 | anchor: A03
A hardship applicant mails proof of hardship with the application to the Driver Services Administrative Office, and approval brings a letter authorizing the application. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec01-F26 | anchor: A03
A hardship applicant must pass vision, knowledge and road tests for a Class D vehicle, adds the Class M knowledge and driving tests to ride a motorcycle, and is then limited to 125 cc. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec01-F27 | anchor: A03
A Class H license is good only during daylight and only for trips to the places named in the approval letter. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec01-F28 | anchor: A03
A hardship license holder who is at least 15 gets the same privileges as a Class PD holder when riding with one of the adults allowed for PD drivers. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec01-F29 | anchor: A03
Every hardship license expires on the holder's 16th birthday, whatever age they were when approved. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec01-F30 | anchor: A03
If a hardship license is approved with less than 6 months left before the 16th birthday, the holder must renew a Class PD at expiration and keep it until reaching 180 days of combined driving experience. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec01-F31 | anchor: A03
An ID-only license involves no testing but demands the same proof of identity and residency as a driver license, and it never authorizes driving. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec01-F32 | anchor: A04
The Expiring Identification License can go to anyone without a valid driver license, and once the holder is 65 or older it no longer expires. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec01-F33 | anchor: A04
A permanent identification license, free and non-expiring, is available to a person who is mentally challenged or physically disabled with a licensed doctor's certified statement that they cannot drive. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec01-F34 | anchor: A04
Driving while your license is revoked, canceled or suspended is a Class B misdemeanor carrying a fine of up to $1,000, up to six months in jail, or both. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec01-F35 | anchor: A04
You must carry your license or TDL whenever you drive and show it to any officer on request; failing to have it is a Class D misdemeanor with a fine from $2 to $50. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec01-F36 | anchor: A04
Non-US citizens working in managerial or technical jobs in Tennessee may drive on another valid license for 6 months and must then apply for a Tennessee license. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec01-F37 | anchor: A04
Anyone under 18 who has dropped out of school before graduating, or who is not making satisfactory progress in school, is not eligible for a license. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec01-F38 | anchor: A04
Applicants who cannot prove US citizenship, lawful permanent residency or temporary legal presence cannot receive a driver license or an ID-only license. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec01-F39 | anchor: A05
TDL class codes begin with the letter X, such as XD, XM and XPD, and a TDL expires on dates tied to the holder's legal presence documents. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec01-F40 | anchor: A05
A Temporary Identification License, shown as Class XID, serves non-driving applicants with temporary legal presence and can be issued for no more than 5 years. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec01-F41 | anchor: A05
Minors aged 13 to 17 who hold a driver license, permit or state ID may register as organ and tissue donors. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec01-F42 | anchor: A06
If no voter registration card arrives within 30 days of applying at a Driver Service Center, contact your County Election Commission right away. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec01-F43 | anchor: A06
A US citizen must be at least 18 and hold a valid license that is not revoked or suspended to obtain an International Driving Permit, which lasts one year from issuance. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0020]

Misconceptions: an International Driving Permit is only a translation and never replaces a valid license; an ID-only license looks like a license but never allows driving; a commercial license already covers passenger cars but not motorcycles; a hardship license is not a general early license and ends at the sixteenth birthday.
Mnemonics: D is for Daily driving, PD is Practice Driving with an adult beside you, H is Hardship with daylight only, M is for Motorcycle, and an X in front means temporary legal presence.
Glossary: TDL means Temporary Driver License for residents with temporary legal presence; GVWR means gross vehicle weight rating; GCWR means gross combination weight rating; For-Hire endorsement means the add-on for people whose main job is driving passengers or property in a Class D vehicle.
Dynamic facts: endorsement fees, the For-Hire fee and the organ-donor and voter procedures are service details that can change; confirm them on the Department of Safety and Homeland Security website before showing them to learners.
